chunks: Abdullah ibn al-Nadr ibn Sam'an al-Taymi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Makki narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Hasan Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Amr al-Atrush al-Harrani narrated to us. He said: Salih ibn Ziyad Abu Shu'ayb al-Susi narrated to us. He said: Abu Thuman al-Sukkari - and his name is Abdullah ibn Maymun - narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Mu'izz al-Awdi narrated to us. He said: Imran ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from Suwayd ibn Ghafla, from Tawus al-Yamani.

He said: I passed by the Hijr and I found a person bowing and prostrating. I observed him, and he was Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). So I said to myself: A righteous man from the People of the House of Prophethood - by Allah, I shall seize his supplication! So I began watching him until he finished his prayer and raised the palms of his hands to the sky, and he began

saying: My Master! My Master! These are my hands that I stretch out to You, filled with sins, and my eyes reach for You with hope. It is right for the one who supplicates to You with regret and humility that You answer him with bounteous generosity.

My Master! Did You create me to be of the people of wretchedness, so that I may prolong my weeping? Or did You create me from the people of happiness, so that my hope may be delighted? My Master! Did You create my limbs to be stricken with rods? Or did You create my intestines to consume boiling water?

My Master! If a slave were able to flee from his master, I would have been the first to flee from You; but I know that I cannot escape You. My Master! If my punishment were something that would expand Your sovereignty, I would have asked You for patience over that. However, I know that the obedience of the obedient does not expand Your sovereignty, and the disobedience of the disobedient does not diminish it.

My Master! What am I, and what is my worth? Forgive my sins with Your grace, dignify me with Your covering, and pardon my reproach with the generosity of Your Face. My God and my Master! Have mercy on me when I lie in agony on my deathbed and my loved ones turn me over. Have mercy on me when I am laid out on the washing place and my righteous neighbours wash me. Have mercy on me when I am carried and my relatives take hold of the edges of my funeral bier. And have mercy on my loneliness, my estrangement, and my solitude in that dark home.

Tawus said: I wept until my wailing intensified. So he turned to me and said: What makes you weep, O Yamani? Or is this not the station of sinners? So I said: My beloved, it is a right upon Allah that He does not turn you away, for your grandfather is Muhammad (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family).

He said: While we were thus, a delegation of his companions came forward. So he turned to them and said: O my companions! I advise you concerning the Hereafter, and I do not advise you concerning this world, for you are already directed by it, covetous of it, and holding fast to it. O my companions! Surely, this world is an abode of passage, while the Hereafter is an abode of permanence. So take from your passage that which will help you in your permanent abode. Do not expose your veils before the One from whom your secrets cannot be hidden. Take your hearts out of this world before your bodies are taken out of it. Have you not seen and heard what was gradually brought upon those before you from the bygone nations and past generations? Do you not see how their hidden matters were exposed, and how the showers of humiliation rained upon them? Their happiness was exchanged after the ease of their livelihood and the softness of their well-being - they became harvests of punishments and stepping-stones of exemplary retributions.
I say this saying of mine and I seek forgiveness from Allah for myself and for you.

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Commander of the Faithful - title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib
key_terms.أهل البيت: Ahlul Bayt - the People of the House, the household of the Prophet Muhammad
key_terms.الحسن والحسين: al-Hasan and al-Husayn - the two grandsons of the Prophet Muhammad
key_terms.الحِجْر: The Hijr - the semi-circular wall near the Ka'ba in Mecca, considered a sacred place of prayer
key_terms.فاطمة: Fatima - daughter of the Prophet Muhammad and wife of Imam Ali

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam Zayn al-Abidin make at the Hijr near the Ka'ba?
ai.summary: Tawus al-Yamani recounts finding Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) praying at the Hijr near the Ka'ba. The Imam delivers a deeply moving supplication to God, expressing his utter dependence and humility - stretching his hands filled with sins, questioning whether he was created for wretchedness or happiness, acknowledging his inability to escape God's power, and pleading for mercy at death. When Tawus weeps, the Imam turns to him and asks why a sinner would not weep at such a place. When companions arrive, the Imam exhorts them to prepare for the Hereafter rather than cling to this fleeting world, warning them with the fate of past nations whose secrets were exposed and whose ease was replaced with punishment.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Abdullah b. al-Nadr b. Sam`an al-Taymi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Abu’l Qasim Ja`far b. Muhammad al-Makki narrated to us. He said: Abu’l Hasan `Abdullah b. Muhammad b. `Amr al-Atrush al-Harrani narrated to us. He said: Salih b. Ziyad Abu Shu`ayb al-Susi narrated to us. He said: Abu Thaman al-Sukri narrated to us – and his name is `Abdullah b. Maymun. He said: `Abdullah b. Mu`iz al-Awdi narrated to us. He said: `Imran b. Sulaym narrated to us from Suwayd b. Ghafla from Tawus al-Yamani.

He said: I passed by a stone and I found a person bowing and prostrating. I looked at him, and I found that it was `Ali b. al-Husayn (as). So, I said to myself: A righteous man from the People of the House of Prophethood. By Allah, I need his supplication. So, I began watching him until he completed his prayer and raised his hands to the sky and said:

My Master! My Master! These are my hands that I stretch out to You, filled with sin. My eyes reach for You in hope. The right of one who supplicates to You in regret and humility is that You answer him with bounteous generosity.

My Master! Did You create me to be of the people of sorrow, so that I may lengthen my weeping; or did You create me from the people of happiness, so that my hope may be delighted? My Master! Did You create my appendages to be stricken with rods? Did You create my gut to consume boiling water?

My Master! Were a slave able to flee from his master, I would [then] be the first to flee from You; but I know that I would not be able to escape You. My Master! If punishing me were to expand Your sovereignty, then I would have asked You for patience over that. However, I know that the obedience of the obedient does not expand Your sovereignty, and the disobedience of the disobedient does not diminish it.

My Master! What am I, and what risk do I pose? Extinguish my errors with Your grace, dignify me with Your covering, and pardon my punishment with the generosity of Your Face. My God and my Master! Forgive me when I am in agony on my deathbed and when my loved ones turn me over. Have mercy on me when I am washed by my righteous neighbours. Have mercy on me when I am carried by my relatives to my funeral. Have mercy on my loneliness, my estrangement, and my solitude in that dark home.

Tawus said: I wept until my wailing intensified. So, he turned to me and said: What makes you weep, Yamani? Or is this not the [correct] status of sinners? So, I said: My beloved! It is a right upon Allah that He answers you, as your grandfather is Muhammad (s).

He said: A delegation of his companions came forward, so he turned to them and said: O my companions! I advise you of the Hereafter, and I do not advise you of this world, for you are directed by it, coveting of it, and holding onto it. O my companions! Surely, this world is a fleeting abode, while the Hereafter is a lasting abode. So, take from your fleeting [abode] that which will help you in your residence. Do not try to hide your secrets from the One from whom they cannot be hidden. Take your hearts out of this world before your bodies are taken out of it. Have you not seen and heard of what has continually accorded to those before you from the earliest nations and the past communities? Do you not see how their secrets were exposed, and how humiliation rained down on them? Their happiness, livelihood, and well-being were exchanged for indignation.
I say this saying of mine, and I repent to Allah for myself and for you.
